name: Prevent Application Removal
description:
Adversaries may abuse the Android device administration API to prevent the user from uninstalling a target application. In earlier versions of Android, device administrator applications needed their administration capabilities explicitly deactivated by the user before the application could be uninstalled. This was later updated so the user could deactivate and uninstall the administrator application in one step.

Adversaries may also abuse the device accessibility APIs to prevent removal. This set of APIs allows the application to perform certain actions on behalf of the user and programmatically determine what is being shown on the screen. The malicious application could monitor the device screen for certain modals (e.g., the confirmation modal to uninstall an application) and inject screen input or a back button tap to close the modal. For example, Android's `performGlobalAction(int)` API could be utilized to prevent the user from removing the malicious application from the device after installation. If the user wants to uninstall the malicious application, two cases may occur, both preventing the user from removing the application.

* Case 1: If the integer argument passed to the API call is `2` or `GLOBAL_ACTION_HOME`, the malicious application may direct the user to the home screen from settings screen 

* Case 2: If the integer argument passed to the API call is `1` or `GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK`, the malicious application may emulate the back press event

telemetry.name: Application Permission
telemetry.description: Declared or granted permissions of a mobile application.
telemetry.collection_focus: Compare manifest declarations with runtime granted state using authorized package inspection and own-app permission checks.

providers.name: Android logcat
providers.scope: Permitted logs from a consented test device/emulator; output depends on build, permissions and instrumentation.

providers.name: Android dumpsys
providers.scope: Point-in-time service/package state on an authorized development device.

providers.name: Instrumented test application
providers.scope: Own-app permission, API and state callbacks; not universal visibility into other apps.

configuration: Use a disposable emulator or owned development device with approved debugging. Record OS/API level, app version and instrumentation privileges.
Collect only relevant logcat buffers/tags and service snapshots; add explicit own-app instrumentation for events absent from OS logs.
Forward sanitized logs and compare before/after state. Remove test data and revoke debugging access after the lab session.

configuration_example.label: Inspect the owned Android lab application
configuration_example.note: Read-only snapshot on a consented debug device. Replace the example package with your owned test app. Output and access vary by Android build; this is not a permission-request event stream.

telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Android tooling does not imply iOS coverage. Standard mobile apps cannot observe all other apps or protected OS internals; MDM status is not full API, filesystem or content telemetry.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per owned device, app version and permission state: unexpected API/permission changes, background activity and network destinations. OS privacy restrictions and emulator differences limit observability.

telemetry.name: OS API Execution
telemetry.description: Instrumented operating-system API calls and their return values.
telemetry.collection_focus: Use an approved EDR trace or instrument the owned lab process at selected APIs. Define API name, caller, sanitized arguments and return status.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

analytics.name: Analytic 1644
analytics.guidance: Correlates (1) an application obtaining or maintaining elevated control mechanisms capable of resisting removal (device administrator, accessibility control, managed-owner posture), (2) user navigation into uninstall or application-management flows, and (3) immediate UI redirection, back-navigation injection, modal dismissal, or failed uninstall completion followed by continued app presence. Defender observes a causal chain where a removal attempt is actively disrupted and the target application remains installed.

tuning.description: Correlation window between uninstall UI entry, interference event, and continued install state
Set of elevated roles considered removal-resistant (device admin, owner modes, accessibility)
UI actions considered suspicious during uninstall flows (BACK, HOME, RECENTS)
Known legitimate accessibility services expected to use global actions
Number of repeated uninstall attempts before escalation
Outbound traffic threshold confirming continued meaningful activity after failed removal

log_sources.name: android:MDMLog
log_sources.channel: application enabled as device administrator, device owner, profile owner, or equivalent elevated management role before uninstall attempt

log_sources.name: android:MDMLog
log_sources.channel: application granted accessibility service privileges capable of screen observation or global action invocation before removal attempt

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: application invokes accessibility global actions (back/home/recents) or observes package-management UI immediately after uninstall/settings screen becomes foreground

mitigations.name: Use Recent OS Version
mitigations.description: Recent versions of Android modified how device administrator applications are uninstalled, making it easier for the user to remove them.

mitigations.name: User Guidance
mitigations.description: Users should be warned against granting access to accessibility features and device administration services, and to carefully scrutinize applications that request these dangerous permissions. Users should be taught how to boot into safe mode to uninstall malicious applications that may be interfering with the uninstallation process.

mitigations.name: Enterprise Policy
mitigations.description: An EMM/MDM can use the Android `DevicePolicyManager.setPermittedAccessibilityServices` method to set an explicit list of applications that are allowed to use Android's accessibility features.
